profile.unsupported_dialects: Explicit root/reference dialect selections fail before codec preparation, with no fallback. The selected codec must reject inconsistent embedded $schema declarations and unsupported required vocabularies.
profile.references: Complete explicit flattened offline resource sets, unique URI within each writer/reader selection. Codec validates URI/$id/anchor/dynamic-reference semantics and rejects missing resources; implicit network retrieval is outside the contract.
profile.compatibility: Encode validates actual serialized JSON against writer. Decode validates the same instance against writer and reader, then deserializes without coercion/default insertion/rewriting. This is per-instance validation, not a global backward/forward compatibility proof.
profile.format: annotation vocabulary; no implicit format assertions
profile.validation_provider: Caller-selected Codec; no built-in JSON parser/serializer/JSON Schema validator added

independent_peer.name: python-jsonschema
independent_peer.numeric_parser: Exact Python integer/Decimal parser; mathematically integral decimal tokens become int before validation; validator unmodified.

behavior_checked: Explicit version/dialect; unsupported root/reference dialects fail before codec calls
Combined writer/reader schema text and URI byte budget, reference-count budget, duplicate/empty resources
Known writer ID, bounded complete frame, UTF-8 and nonempty document checks
Validation of actual serialized payload; partial writes/reads and overflow cannot return success
Writer and reader checks run before decoding; failure stops subsequent codec work
Null is literal JSON, default annotation does not rewrite it, boolean schemas are delegated explicitly
Exact int64 min/max, above-f64 integer, decimal boundary representations, exponent integer/fraction forms
Fractional/out-of-range/wrong-type, NaN/Infinity, leading zero and trailing/missing JSON rejection
Reader constraint differences preserve codec validation failure without automatic compatibility assumptions

limits: JSON parsing, JSON Schema semantics, URI/reference resolution and value serialization are delegated to the explicitly selected production Codec. No production built-in validator is claimed.
The checked-in Rust codec recognizes only the fixture schemas and their scalar numeric constraints; it is not a general-purpose JSON Schema implementation.
Input/frame/schema bounds do not constrain arbitrary codec-internal parsing work, scratch, retained schemas, object allocation or RSS; callers must configure those separately.
Independent verification covers offline representative schemas/instances and actual Rust frame output, not live Schema Registry/Kafka interoperability or complete ecosystem qualification.
Reference oracle rpds-py wheel is pinned for Python 3.12/Linux x86_64; another platform needs a separate reviewed peer wheel pin.
The feature is opt-in, adds no Rust dependency and performs no lookup, publication, registration or registry mutation.
